issue.title: Feature: support remote Streamable HTTP MCP servers in octet-mcp
issue.mutability: Issue text is mutable; original Wix reproduction remains historical, not a current live result.

baseline_policy.scope: First-class MCP client qualification, not a Shopify adapter. Preserve actual baseline-supported resources and standard elicitation and explicitly distinguish protocol optionals not exposed by baseline.
baseline_policy.codex_mode_caveat: Pinned Codex defaults to legacy; modern mode is under-development opt-in. Public protocol requirements and Codex implementation evidence are distinct, neither is blanket conformance proof.

status_meaning.implemented: Present for the specifically described pinned-snapshot scope; not a release/live pass.
status_meaning.partial: Some source behavior exists but substantive gaps or known defects remain.
status_meaning.missing: No usable implementation of the described behavior in pinned Octet; optional rows may correctly remain unsupported.
status_meaning.needs-live-evidence: Product/endpoint qualification cannot be established from source or controlled fixtures.

baseline_policy.evidence_rule: Tests listed in source were inspected, not run here. Parent may append candidate evidence/update current_octet assessments after actual runs; retain immutable input snapshot and upstream scope.
baseline_policy.security_rule: Preserve exact endpoint trust, host-derived owner fences, fail-closed tool policy and no ambiguous automatic action replay even where upstream retry guidance is more permissive.

OCTET.assessment: Input snapshot, before the implementation stack; not a statement about later working-tree edits.

RMCP.inspection: Read verified archive in memory only; no dependency installation or extraction.

sources.finding: Legacy is the default; modern selects Auto discovery with a 2025-06-18 fallback. Stdio additionally requires its explicit protocol marker.
mcp_2026_07_28 and coordinated OAuth refresh are UnderDevelopment and default disabled.
The client enables rmcp auth, client, async-rw, child-process and Streamable HTTP features; this is not evidence that every SDK feature is exposed by Codex.
rmcp 3.2.0 registry archive checksum pins the delegated protocol implementation.

Typed tool and resource operations, bearer/header/OAuth transports, custom requests, modern MRTR selection, disabled SDK response cache, legacy session-expiry recovery; transient operation retries are limited to tools/list.
Constructs default client capabilities, adds elicitation and selected extensions; does not advertise roots or sampling.
Product connection manager lists paginated resources/templates and reads resources, not just an unused SDK declaration.
Forwards elicitation to the user callback and receives progress/log/list-change notifications. It does not implement sampling or application roots; prompt-list logging is not a prompts UI.
Handles standard elicitation plus explicitly enabled OpenAI forms/user verification, delegates remaining requests to the ordinary handler.
Drives bounded input-required rounds, constructs input responses and retains opaque request state; this is a semantic continuation, not a blind transport retry.
Fixtures assert self-contained metadata, standard/custom headers and invalid header-schema exclusion, correlated version evidence and bounded legacy fallback. Test source was inspected, not executed.
Fixtures drive form/URL elicitation, resources/read and opaque state-only rounds. Test source is not an Octet result.
Delegates authorization discovery to AuthorizationManager and includes protected-resource metadata challenge coverage; ordinary legacy mode allows absent issuer metadata.
Checks authorization requests exclude resource headers; legacy GET-first discovery, missing-issuer compatibility and explicit issuer mismatch rejection.
Advertised CIMD is selected only for supported public-client authentication and loopback callback shape; DCR remains fallback and explicit modes exist.
Browser callback validates issuer before code exchange; supports pre-registered client, stores issuer even without refresh token. Legacy missing-issuer allowance is explicit.
Redirects are bounded to original origin and a shared timeout; some POST redirects become bodyless GET. Octet may remain stricter rather than copy this policy.
Explicitly trusted IdP credential exchanges an ID-JAG assertion for a resource-bound MCP bearer; no implicit interactive login or resource discovery in this primitive.
Enterprise logout invalidates concurrent login generations and credential persistence revalidates current account/configuration under a lock.

Removes initialization, protocol sessions, resumability and server requests; adds stateless metadata, discovery, subscriptions, MRTR, headers, cache hints and wider schemas. Roots, sampling, logging and DCR are deprecated, not all removed.
Normative TypeScript message shapes: required request metadata/result discriminator; input-required state; capabilities; cache hints; arbitrary JSON structured output and general schema keywords.
Request-scoped version selection, modern errors and transport-specific dual-era interoperability; discovery is mandatory for servers, optional for clients.
server/discover returns supportedVersions/capabilities plus optional metadata identity/instructions and cache hints; serverInfo is not security authority.
Modern servers do not send JSON-RPC requests. Dual-era stdio probes discovery and falls back on a non-modern error or bounded silence; cancellation/shutdown remain transport-specific.
POST JSON/SSE, per-request headers and safe parameter mirroring, stream-close cancellation; modern mode has no Mcp-Session-Id, GET/DELETE session lifecycle or Last-Event-ID.
Input-required is allowed on tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get only; retry uses new ID and exact opaque state, confined to original operation.
subscriptions/listen opts into filters, requires first acknowledgment and subscriptionId demultiplexing, and is re-established after reconnect.
Modern HTTP closes response stream; stdio sends cancellation notification; late responses and bounded maximum timeouts remain explicit.
Cacheable results carry ttlMs/cacheScope; caching is optional and private reuse is bound to authorization context; MRTR continuations cannot be cached.
Catalogs may vary by authorization, not connection; schema/header rules, resource links/embedded resources and arbitrary JSON structured content are not tools-only text.
Issuer-bound callbacks, resource indicators, bearer tokens, optional refresh issuance and scope-challenge/step-up handling.
Both challenge and path/root well-known protected-resource discovery; ordered OAuth/OIDC issuer discovery; exact issuer validation and separate registration state.
Pre-registration, advertised CIMD, deprecated DCR fallback with application_type; client credentials keyed to issuing authorization server.
PKCE S256 and metadata support checks, secure storage, token audience/resource separation and no token passthrough.
Shipped snapshot: local stdio, blocked experimental HTTP, no stock OAuth/resources/prompts/sampling/elicitation.
Nine retained defects, inert owner-only gate, unavailable stock credentials, legacy framing/recovery, policy, catalogs/media, semantic presentation and fixture-only tests.
Offers 2025-06-18 and only 2025-03-26/2024-11-05 alternatives, initialize/initialized, empty client capabilities and rejects all reverse server requests.
Initializes legacy HTTP sessions, lists tools and routes legacy notifications/cancellation; not modern stateless lifecycle.

Conservative annotation policy, schema vocabulary filter/basic validation and text/image/audio result lowering; arbitrary structured JSON already serializes, but full schema semantics and resource content are not supported.
API 0.3 does not imply dynamic tools, legacy UI/brokers or image/audio support. MCP wire and host extension API are separate.
Coding product offers no approvals/secrets broker; resource ownership must come from host, and input cancellation is fail-closed.
Existing real subprocess, cancellation, timeout/no replay and bounded descendant shutdown regressions; not executed by baseline author.
Existing deterministic loopback legacy session/bearer/resume/no-replay/no-adapter fixtures; not production or OAuth qualification.
Existing media/catalog epochs, no replay and pre-worker experimental gate fixtures.
Default sampling is method-not-found; roots default to an empty list. Codex does not advertise either capability or replace these with model/workspace integration.
SDK supports subscriptions/listen and prompts/get/MRTR helpers; availability in this dependency is not proof the Codex wrapper/product exposes them.

matrix.feature: Explicit local stdio configuration and resident lifecycle
matrix.codex_support: Supported local child/executor transports; exact Codex launch syntax is not the parity contract.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Stdio process framing, stderr, cancellation and EOF shutdown remain supported.

current_octet.assessment: Verify shipped stdio; do not rebuild it or add installation/ambient discovery. Real subprocess fixture evidence still needs a candidate run.

matrix.codex_support: Legacy default; 2026 mode is under-development opt-in; stdio additionally opts in. Modern fallback includes server-selected 2025-11-25.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Modern requests select a version per request; recognized modern errors must not cause blind legacy downgrade.

current_octet.assessment: Only legacy 2025-06-18/2025-03-26/2024-11-05 accepted. Need era-specific negotiation, bounded probes, modern-error handling and 2025-11-25 compatibility, not a constant substitution.

matrix.feature: Stateless server discovery and per-request metadata
matrix.codex_support: 2026 mode drives server/discover and SDK self-contained requests; not the default mode.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: No initialize/initialized in modern mode. Required protocolVersion/clientCapabilities in _meta, optional client/server identity; discover returns supportedVersions/capabilities/cache hints.

current_octet.assessment: Implement modern startup and request construction, identity/capability parsing and resultType validation. Do not confuse protocol discovery at an explicit endpoint with ambient server discovery.

matrix.codex_support: Modern fixture asserts standard headers and rejects invalid x-mcp-header schemas.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, matching MCP-Protocol-Version/_meta, safe Mcp-Param-* mirroring and sentinel Base64 encoding required.

current_octet.assessment: Retain and validate x-mcp-header schema annotations, case-insensitive uniqueness/static property reachability and allowed primitives; omit absent/null, encode Unicode/control/sentinel/edge whitespace. No arbitrary credential header invention.

matrix.feature: Streamable HTTP POST with JSON and SSE responses
matrix.codex_support: Typed StreamableHttpClientTransport with auth, bounded startup and response handling.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Both application/json and text/event-stream; notifications receive bodyless 202; correlate request-scoped SSE, reject invalid frames.

current_octet.assessment: Experimental legacy implementation exists, but nine defects and missing modern semantics block production. A loopback response is not internet/TLS qualification.

matrix.feature: Legacy session IDs, expiration and fresh-session recovery
matrix.codex_support: Legacy session-expired 404 is classified separately and reinitializes a serialized replacement transport.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: 2025-era session/GET/DELETE/resume behavior is legacy only. Modern 404 method-not-found is not session expiration.

current_octet.assessment: Legacy session identity and 404 recovery exist experimentally; qualify owner/auth isolation, teardown and optional stream behavior. Must not mint/forward session or resume state in 2026 mode.

matrix.codex_support: Retries transient tools/list; has legacy session-expiry recovery and elicitation-aware timeouts, not unconditional tool retries.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Modern HTTP cancel closes stream; stdio uses notifications/cancelled. Broken modern streams cannot resume; any newly authorized retry uses a new ID.

current_octet.assessment: Keep stricter Octet prohibition on automatic ambiguous tool replay. Separate explicit MRTR continuation, safe catalog retry, legacy event resume and modern stream loss; retain one end-to-end deadline and tombstone late replies.

matrix.codex_support: rmcp SDK offers listen with acknowledgment; reviewed Codex wrapper exposes no first-class listen method and ordinary list-change callbacks only log. Do not infer product support from SDK.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: subscriptions/listen replaces standalone GET and resources/subscribe/unsubscribe. Filter acknowledgment, subscriptionId demultiplexing and cancellation/re-establishment are core patterns.

current_octet.assessment: Need bounded long-lived POST-response subscriptions, acknowledgment validation, owner/ID routing and re-establishment. Legacy tools/list_changed callback alone is insufficient.

matrix.feature: Tool catalogs, pagination and pinned call schemas
matrix.codex_support: Typed tools/list and call plus product catalog snapshots.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Bounded pagination; modern catalogs may vary by authorization but not connection.

current_octet.assessment: Existing bounded/cycle-checked legacy catalogs, transactional dynamic registration and epoch-pinned schemas should be verified unchanged. Modern freshness/authorization behavior belongs to MCP-010.

matrix.feature: Catalog freshness and cache authorization partition
matrix.codex_support: Codex explicitly disables rmcp response caching/stale-on-error, preserving product snapshots. Do not require enabling SDK caching for parity.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Cacheable results include ttlMs/cacheScope. Caching optional; private reuse stays in same authorization context and MRTR continuations cannot be cached.

current_octet.assessment: Existing epochs are not 2026 cache semantics. Handle cache hints/missing legacy fields and ensure catalog invalidation across owner/token changes; choosing no response cache is valid.

matrix.feature: General tool schemas and structured JSON output
matrix.codex_support: Uses rmcp typed tool/results; input arguments must remain objects. Wider wire types do not prove full provider-side JSON Schema conformance.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Input root remains object, with composition/conditional/$ref/$defs keywords; outputSchema and structuredContent can describe any JSON value.

current_octet.assessment: Octet already serializes arbitrary structured JSON, but filters schema vocabulary and validates only a basic subset. Need bounded reference/composition semantics and lossless contract handling or explicit rejection; never silently weaken validation.

matrix.feature: Text, image/audio and resource-bearing tool results
matrix.codex_support: Typed CallToolResult retains MCP content; resource APIs are exposed separately. Verify per-frontend rendering rather than infer all model modalities.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Ordered text/image/audio/resource links/embedded resources, structuredContent and isError are distinct result channels.

current_octet.assessment: Text/image/audio/artifacts and bounded structured data exist. Embedded resources/resource links are rejected; schema-less structured data is metadata only. Qualify provenance, model visibility and artifact ownership; do not claim all content parity.

matrix.codex_support: Product manager and rmcp wrapper implement resources/list, resources/templates/list and resources/read, including modern read MRTR.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Optional server capability, but genuinely supported by chosen Codex baseline.

current_octet.assessment: Must implement first-class bounded resource/template discovery/read and content conversion with owner fences. Cannot exclude resources merely because initial Octet bridge was tools-only.

matrix.codex_support: No typed prompts/list, prompts/get or completion product surface in reviewed rmcp wrapper/connection manager; generic custom requests and SDK get_prompt are not first-class support.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Optional server prompts/completions; prompts/get uses MRTR when implemented.

current_octet.assessment: Do not advertise prompts/completions. Keep visible in matrix as protocol optional, not a proven Codex product parity gap; reconsider only with specific exposed call-site evidence.

matrix.codex_support: Standard elicitation callback and form-mode MRTR fixture genuinely execute the client-side exchange.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Optional capability; 2026 inputRequests carries elicitation/create, not reverse JSON-RPC requests.

current_octet.assessment: Need host-correlated user input/schema validation, accept/decline/cancel, bounded pending requests and headless denial. Form fields are not permission grants and must not collect secrets.

matrix.feature: URL-mode elicitation and manual out-of-band interaction
matrix.codex_support: Standard URL mode is exercised alongside form mode; optional custom OpenAI verification is separate.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: 2026 removes elicitationId/elicitation-complete; retry of original MRTR operation learns outcome.

current_octet.assessment: Need explicit manual URL interaction, provenance and cancellation without auto-navigation/login or promoting server URL to trusted authority. Not equivalent to MCP transport OAuth.

matrix.codex_support: Modern tools/call and resources/read drive input-required rounds, including state-only and metadata-bearing replies.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Validate resultType; input-required only on eligible methods; preserve opaque requestState exactly, use new ID, do not leak state across concurrent calls.

current_octet.assessment: Without explicit resultType handling, current lowerer can reduce input-required to empty successful content. Add discriminator validation, capability-checked input handlers, bounded rounds/bytes/time and state-only backoff; no blind replay.

matrix.codex_support: Capabilities do not advertise sampling; handler inherits method-not-found. SDK sampling types do not supply Codex model-session integration.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Optional and deprecated, not removed, in 2026; modern interaction would use MRTR.

current_octet.assessment: Do not add unsolicited model invocation or advertise sampling. Unsupported is not a parity defect for this exposed baseline; maintain explicit refusal tests.

matrix.codex_support: Not advertised; default SDK handler returns empty roots, not a Codex workspace-root integration.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Optional and deprecated in 2026; roots/list_changed removed.

current_octet.assessment: No ambient workspace disclosure or advertised roots capability. Keep separate from internal Codex capability-root terminology.

matrix.codex_support: Logging handler receives progress/log/change notifications; receiving is not catalog invalidation or a prompt UI.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Modern request-scoped notifications and per-request logLevel; logging is deprecated, logging/setLevel and ping removed.

current_octet.assessment: Retain bounded numeric/redacted presentation. Add modern request/subscription correlation and no-unrequested-logging behavior; do not carry legacy heartbeat/log methods into modern mode.

matrix.codex_support: Constructors support unauthenticated, bearer and configured headers plus OAuth. Octet need not copy secret-bearing Codex configuration syntax.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: HTTP may be unauthenticated or authenticated; credentials remain endpoint/resource-bound, never URL query tokens.

current_octet.assessment: Unauth path and narrow request-scoped bearer adapter exist experimentally; stock runtime has no provider. Need first-class owner-bound credential plumbing while retaining no ambient secret/env/header inheritance.

matrix.codex_support: AuthorizationManager handles protected-resource challenges; tests separate OAuth discovery from starting an MCP protocol session and strip resource headers.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Support WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata then path/root RFC9728, OAuth RFC8414/OIDC ordered discovery and exact issuer validation.

current_octet.assessment: 401/403 generic parking is not auth discovery. Implement bounded untrusted metadata traversal, origin/resource/issuer validation and no credential forwarding to discovery destinations; preserve explicit endpoint trust.

matrix.feature: OAuth PKCE, callback and consent lifecycle
matrix.codex_support: Interactive browser callback/code exchange, pre-registered client and issuer validation are implemented.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: OAuth 2.1, S256 PKCE support checks, exact redirect/state and optional-present iss validation before code exchange, resource indicators.

current_octet.assessment: Need first-class manually authorized login/cancel/expiry callback flow bound to active host owner; never model-driven login or code/token data in tools, logs, sessions or this matrix.

matrix.feature: Client registration: pre-registered, CIMD and legacy DCR
matrix.codex_support: Supports configured client ID, Auto/Cimd/Dcr selection and advertised public-client CIMD with validated callback; DCR fallback.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Prefer existing pre-registration, then advertised CIMD; DCR deprecated fallback requires appropriate application_type, and credentials bind to issuer.

current_octet.assessment: Need all supported registration journeys; DCR-only or static bearer integration is not full baseline auth. Octet CIMD needs its own reviewed HTTPS metadata identity; never reuse Codex client ID.

matrix.feature: Credential ownership, issuer/resource binding, refresh and logout
matrix.codex_support: Stored issuer and managed OAuth credentials/refresh; separate under-development coordinated refresh mode; enterprise logout uses generation fencing.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Separate authorization-server registration state; audience/resource indicators, private token storage and no assumption a refresh token exists; appropriate scope challenge handling.

current_octet.assessment: Implement secure stock store/provider, refresh rotation/rejection and logout/relogin, concurrent refresh fences and endpoint/owner/account isolation. Missing issuer allowance in Codex legacy mode is not permission to weaken current MCP requirements.

matrix.codex_support: Codex user-interaction machinery is not Octet authorization. Parity must preserve Octet host enforcement.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Tools security requires treating annotations as untrusted and allowing human denial of sensitive actions.

current_octet.assessment: Only exact uncontradicted readOnlyHint true bypasses extra policy. Unknown/destructive remains denied without negotiated host approval. #383 is separate; public/authenticated reachability never approves a write. Positive approved-write journey stays blocked until host issuance exists.

matrix.feature: Remote transport/owner safety and bounded cleanup
matrix.codex_support: Pinned upstream limits/redirect behavior are reference evidence, not a substitute for Octet resource ownership and stricter network policy.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Untrusted network/metadata/auth channels require confidentiality, safe validation and bounded transport work.

current_octet.assessment: Retained nine-defect ledger remains release-blocking until each remediation has targeted evidence. Production cannot be unlocked by fixture count or protocol constant changes.

matrix.feature: First-class product setup/status and frontend ownership
matrix.codex_support: Parity means equivalent usable client journeys, not embedding MCP into the Octet kernel or copying Codex UI.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: MCP transport is independent from host extension API/frontend.

current_octet.assessment: Existing /mcp lifecycle, semantic state and API 0.2 artifacts have deterministic fixtures. Need shipped candidate TUI/Serve/headless evidence, owner switching and inert installation; do not retag API 0.3.

matrix.codex_support: Reviewed constructors/build features expose stdio and Streamable HTTP, not retired transport-sse-client. SSE POST response tests are not standalone SSE support.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: 2024 HTTP+SSE is deprecated; optional backward compatibility must be distinguished from ordinary Streamable HTTP SSE.

current_octet.assessment: Keep explicit unsupported diagnostic; do not infer a legacy endpoint-event adapter is required from Codex Streamable HTTP filenames.

matrix.codex_support: SDK types/default callbacks and generic custom requests exist, but no first-class public tasks operation is established in reviewed wrapper.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Tasks moved out of core into io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks; extensions are explicitly advertised, not implied by protocol version.

current_octet.assessment: Keep core capability set honest; no task/background execution promises from merely recognizing extensions metadata.

matrix.codex_support: Actual ID-JAG resource-token exchange and issuer/account/generation-bound enterprise login/logout primitives are present.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Not mandatory core authorization; an additional enterprise authorization mechanism with separate trust/policy configuration.

current_octet.assessment: Retained baseline-supported conditional surface, not silently called unsupported upstream. Requires separate substantive implementation and authorized enterprise evidence before claiming this capability or unqualified entire-Codex parity. Not needed to prove unauthenticated Shopify.

matrix.feature: Codex-specific forms/user verification and app extensions
matrix.codex_support: Capability-checked OpenAI forms and user-verification requests are implemented; generic app metadata can be advertised. This does not establish all GUI app support in all Codex frontends.
matrix.public_mcp_requirement: Non-core extension contracts; standard form/URL elicitation remains independently required for baseline parity.

current_octet.assessment: Inventory explicitly, do not mislabel as protocol-mandatory or implemented Octet capability. OpenAI-native verification/app behavior is not a substitute for standard elicitation and would need separately scoped host/UI work if claimed.

journeys.target: Existing reviewed local stdio server, not newly installed software
steps: Run existing real subprocess suite; initialize/list/call/refresh/restart/stop.
Exercise pagination, epochs, text/structured/media, cancellation/timeout/crash and descendant shutdown.
Verify unchanged behavior through the actual candidate host with a reviewed already-installed server.
required_evidence: Candidate commit/build/package hashes, command, platform and exact test names/outcomes.
Owner-fenced tool/result trace and process-cleanup observation; no secrets.
journeys.blocker: Candidate runs belong to implementing parent; no tests executed by source-baseline author.

journeys.target: Pinned modern, legacy and dual-era controlled fixtures
steps: Verify 2024-11-05/2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25 legacy compatibility without advertising unsupported semantics.
Modern stdio and HTTP discover return JSON/SSE, with/without serverInfo; all requests carry required _meta; no initialize on modern wire.
Probe error/silence, modern -32020/-32021/-32022, valid/invalid supported lists and mismatched IDs; auth rejection cannot manufacture downgrade.
required_evidence: Wire transcripts recording selected era/version and explicit fallback reason.
Negative fixtures for unknown resultType, capabilities, unsupported version and per-request isolation.
journeys.blocker: Modern lifecycle and 2025-11-25 compatibility are missing in the pinned Octet snapshot.

steps: Verify method/name/version body-header equivalence and x-mcp-header on static nested properties.
Reject duplicate/invalid annotation names, arrays/$ref/composition placement and unsupported primitives without exposing invalid tools.
Verify Unicode/control/sentinel/leading whitespace encoding, optional absent/null and safe integer limits; schema change forces safe refresh.
required_evidence: Captured headers and schema acceptance/rejection without secret values.
Proof malformed header schema cannot inject Authorization or arbitrary HTTP fields.
journeys.blocker: No modern header schema pipeline in pinned Octet.

journeys.target: Loopback-only controlled legacy/modern JSON and SSE fixtures
steps: Single messages, accepted content types/202, notifications and terminal response identity.
Legacy session establishment/change/expiry/termination versus modern no-session/no-resume/no-GET lifecycle.
Malformed/truncated UTF-8/JSON/SSE/chunks/Content-Length, empty event IDs and request-scoped control-message flood.
required_evidence: Focused test IDs and redacted bounded wire observations; no passing count alone.
Aggregate byte/event/thread/time limits through all error/resume/auth paths.
journeys.blocker: Nine legacy safety defects plus missing modern semantics; fixtures alone never satisfy G-LIVE.

journeys.target: Controlled DNS/network doubles and two independently host-derived owners
steps: Rebinding/private/link-local address rejection, reviewed-address pinning and TLS hostname verification.
No cross-owner/endpoint/issuer/token/session/catalog/SSE identity reuse; generation and account switches retire stale authority.
DNS and socket cancellation/shutdown bounds, fanout caps, non-resettable aggregate budgets and startup absolute deadline.
required_evidence: One targeted evidence item for every D-HTTP-01 through D-HTTP-09.
Adversarial denial records prove no credentials, queries, raw logs or sensitive headers reach another destination/owner.
journeys.blocker: Retained ledger remains unqualified until fixes and targeted candidate tests are recorded.

steps: List paginated tools/resources/templates and read a selected resource, retaining exact endpoint/server provenance.
Validate general input/output schemas and all supported content parts; malicious descriptions stay data.
Exercise modern subscription acknowledgment/filter/ID routing, catalog changes, private authorization cache invalidation and reconnect.
required_evidence: No silent omitted features; resource/template operations and content model visibility observed through host.
Bounded schema/reference tests and complete dynamic catalog/epoch outcomes.
journeys.blocker: Resources, subscriptions and wider content/schema semantics need implementation.

journeys.target: Reviewed server requesting standard form/URL input
steps: Legacy reverse elicitation and modern tools/call/resources/read MRTR; accept/decline/cancel with host-derived parent owner.
Multiple input keys, state-only rounds, opaque Unicode/newline state, missing/unknown resultType and unsupported capabilities.
Manual URL opening/login only after owner consent; headless unavailable input denies; timeout/cancel cannot leak continuation to another owner.
required_evidence: Exact terminal disposition, bounded round/byte/time count and state equality without recording sensitive state.
Proof no sampling/root request is advertised or fulfilled as model authority.
journeys.blocker: No stock elicitation/MRTR implementation in pinned Octet; no user/auth interactions authorized for this worker.

journeys.target: Controlled protected resource + independent authorization/OIDC servers
steps: 401 challenge resource_metadata, path and root well-known fallback; OAuth/OIDC issuer paths in required order.
Exact issuer mismatch, resource binding, scopes, PKCE S256 metadata, redirects, malicious metadata and callback iss/state mismatches fail closed.
Pre-registered client, advertised CIMD and DCR fallback with native application_type; no resource Authorization/header values leak to discovery or another issuer.
required_evidence: Captured request destinations, registration mode and denial classifications with all secrets removed.
No fallback to legacy protocol merely because authentication failed.
journeys.blocker: Stock OAuth/discovery/registration are missing; vendor 404 documentation lookups are not auth evidence.

journeys.target: Explicitly authorized generic remote resource and user-held OAuth account
steps: Owner initiates login and manual browser consent; code exchange, resource-bound token use and supported scopes.
Cancel/deny/expired/wrong callback; restart with secure store; no-refresh-token grant and refresh rotation/failure.
Revocation/logout/relogin, concurrent refresh, changed issuer/account/owner and insufficient_scope; never replay ambiguous action.
required_evidence: Dated sanitized session reference, endpoint/issuer identity, candidate hashes, registration mode and auth/session/recovery outcomes.
No tokens, codes, PKCE verifier, cookies or account identifiers in committed evidence.
journeys.blocker: Requires implementing client, approved credential store/identity and human authorization. Do not run automatically.

journeys.target: Controlled failures plus harmless calls on an authorized remote server
steps: Cancel/timeout/disconnect before and after request transmission, with progress and delayed terminal responses.
Legacy SSE cursor resume without re-POST and legacy session-expired 404; modern request loss uses no Last-Event-ID/session headers.
Bound catalog retry/backoff/429, no unsafe automatic tools/call retry, generation retirement and fresh modern subscription after reconnect.
required_evidence: Request ID/method counts and terminal ambiguity; prove no duplicate tool side effect.
Bounds survive every transport and authentication branch.
journeys.blocker: Modern/remote safety and authenticated real session evidence remain open.

steps: Connect through generic octet-mcp configuration with auth omitted, not a Shopify-only adapter.
Observe actual era/version/catalog; run only an approved harmless read with required policy and record output provenance.
Observe cancellation/reconnect where safely reproducible; stop without purchase/cart mutation or customer login.
required_evidence: Exact user-selected storefront endpoint, dated sanitized session/build references and observed tool names/version/transport.
Record authentication_required rather than adding credentials if the public endpoint challenges.
journeys.blocker: No storefront supplied and no endpoint calls authorized. This is the requested unauthenticated storefront journey, not OAuth proof.

steps: Qualify separately through the same generic client with auth omitted.
Observe UCP MCP discovery/catalog and harmless authorized read; do not substitute ordinary /api/mcp results or non-MCP UCP metadata.
Keep cart/checkout/order/payment mutations blocked without separate approval.
required_evidence: Independent exact endpoint and sanitized session record, observed protocol and supported tool journey.
journeys.blocker: No storefront supplied or endpoint calls authorized; /api/mcp success cannot mark this path passed.

steps: Retain original #179 remote setup goal; use current native Octet config rather than treating historical mcpServers syntax as new compatibility requirement.
User manually authorizes required Wix account flow, then list and invoke one harmless appropriately approved operation.
Observe supported token/session expiry, reconnect/cancel and logout/revocation without leaking account data.
required_evidence: Authenticated dated session and candidate hashes; actual endpoint protocol/auth mode/scopes and result/cancellation outcomes.
If Wix has changed or account access is unavailable, record the exact blocker; never replace with unauthenticated Shopify evidence.
journeys.blocker: Historical issue endpoint only; current service/auth/account behavior unverified. No login or endpoint calls authorized.

journeys.target: Explicit customer-account resource selected and authorized by its owner; not inferred from storefront paths
steps: First demonstrate the generic OAuth client; separately review the customer resource, issuer and scopes.

retained_http_defects.title: DNS rebinding / HTTPS SSRF
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Validate all resolved addresses and pin connections to approved public addresses while preserving TLS hostname verification; test rebinding and private/link-local targets.

retained_http_defects.title: Cross-owner credential/session state
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Partition all credential, protocol session, cursor/catalog and continuation state by exact resource plus host-derived owner/generation; retire on change.

retained_http_defects.title: DNS workers outlive cancellation/shutdown
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Use cancellable/isolated bounded resolution with observable cleanup; no orphan DNS work may escape process/owner shutdown.

retained_http_defects.title: Buffered SSE peer-identity confusion
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Validate originating request/session/owner before dispatching every buffered event and reject foreign terminal/control messages.

retained_http_defects.title: Unbounded control-message fanout
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Bound reverse/control message scheduling, queues and threads; rejected overflow remains a bounded error.

retained_http_defects.title: Resettable aggregate budgets
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Carry one byte/event/request/time accounting scope across redirects/auth/discovery/SSE/resume/recovery; no fresh per-path allowance.

retained_http_defects.title: Accepted truncated framing
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Reject short Content-Length/chunks/SSE/JSON/UTF-8 and unterminated frames; never mistake truncated content for terminal success.

retained_http_defects.title: Incorrect empty SSE event-ID cursor
retained_http_defects.acceptance: Legacy empty id resets cursor, not old-ID reuse; modern mode ignores/removes resume machinery entirely.

retained_http_defects.title: Escapable startup deadline
retained_http_defects.acceptance: One absolute deadline spans credentials/DNS/connect/TLS/handshake/catalog and all retries; no stage resets it.
